lesson_title: The Toll Gate Hiding Inside Every Battery
hook_text: Your battery reads full voltage and still won't work. It isn't lying — it's charging you a toll.
clip_script: Picture the battery as a depot with one exit gate, and at the gate stands a toll collector who never sleeps. The depot promises a certain push to every parcel of charge it sends out — that promise is the emf. But no parcel leaves without passing the gate, and the collector takes a cut as it goes by. What actually arrives at the terminals is the promise minus the cut. The toll has one merciful rule: no traffic, no charge. That is why an old torch cell reads full voltage on a multimeter — zero current, zero toll — and then barely glows in the torch, because the moment real current tries to leave, the aged chemistry's swollen toll gate confiscates most of the push. And it is why headlights droop when a car cranks: the starter motor is a huge, greedy parallel branch, the current surges, the toll surges with it, and the lamps wired across the terminals feel the sag — resistance down, current up, lost volts up, terminal voltage down, four links every time. Mechanics exploit this daily: a battery that reads healthy at rest but collapses under cranking has an extortionate internal toll, and no charger can bribe it away. Emf is the promise. Terminal voltage is the delivery. The difference is the toll — and now you can calculate it.
visual_style: A depot gate with a toll collector skimming glowing charge parcels; a multimeter reading full volts beside a dim torch; car headlights sagging as a starter motor branch snaps into a circuit diagram, four chain links lighting up in sequence.
mood: Detective reveal — the hidden charge inside every battery, exposed step by step.
pacing: Toll-gate metaphor setup, torch mystery, headlight surge with the four-link chain, mechanic's-verdict close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and audit any battery's budget in your final exams.
